At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, Śakra, Brahmā, and the Four Heavenly Kings rose from their seats, joined their palms in reverence, prostrated at the feet of Śākyamuni Buddha, and addressed him, saying:
“World-Honored One!”

We, the great assembly, have all now heard of the supreme merits of the original vows of all Buddhas, and we have witnessed the arrival here of the Buddhas' compassion, which has enabled us sentient beings to personally receive their offerings.

"Bhagavān! If, in any place, this sūtra, as well as the names of the seven Buddhas and the dhāraṇī methods, are circulated, honored, or even committed to writing, we shall all, by virtue of the Buddha’s majestic power, go to that place to protect those [who uphold them]."

May kings, ministers, cities, towns, and villages, as well as men and women, not be afflicted by manifold sufferings or various diseases; may they always attain peace and security, with abundant wealth and food.
"We shall thus repay the kindness of all Buddhas.
World-Honored One!
In the presence of the Buddha, we ourselves have made this solemn vow:"
"If there are men or women of pure faith who keep me in mind, they should recite this mantra.
He then spoke the mantra:

*Tadyathā | a-kū-mo-kū | tra-kū | ma-ma-kū-ku-sai | ha-hu-he | ma-ra-ma-ra-ma-ra | kin-tsu-sai-pu-sai | Svāhā.* "If there are men or women of pure faith—whether kings, princes, ministers, high officials, members of the inner court, or ladies-in-waiting—who recite the names of the Seven Buddhas and this divine mantra, and who read, copy, and reverently make offerings to them, shall all in this present life obtain freedom from illness and long life; they shall be free from all suffering and affliction, shall not fall into the three miserable realms, shall attain the stage of non-retrogression, and shall proceed even unto Bodhi."

In those various Buddha-lands, they take birth according to their wishes, constantly behold all Buddhas, and attain the knowledge of past lives; in mindfulness, concentration, and dhāraṇī, there is nothing they do not fully possess.
"If one suffers from diseases such as demonic malaria, one should write this mantra and tie it behind the elbow; once the illness has been cured, place it in a clean location.
At that time, the Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva went to the abodes of the seven Buddhas, circumambulated them three times to the right, paid his respects to each, and said:
"World-Honored One!"
I pray that you, out of your compassion, will protect and keep me in mind; for the sake of benefiting future men and women who uphold this sutra, I shall now further recite for them a dhāraṇī mantra.
Then those seven Buddhas praised Vajradhara, saying:
“Excellent! Excellent!”
Vajrapāṇi! I shall empower you;
you may now proclaim this divine mantra to protect those who uphold this sutra in the future, so that they may be free from all afflictions and have their aspirations fulfilled.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi spoke this mantra:

*Namāḥ samantabhadrebhyaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhebhyaḥ | Namāḥ sarvavajradharebhyaḥ | Tadyathā | Oṃ vajraśe vajraśe mahāvajraśe vajrapāśa dhāraya samaya samaya samantābhyantara vajraśe śama śama prasaumye sarvavidyā kuru kuru sarvakarma āvaraṇaṃ nikṣipa samayamanu smara bhagavan vajrapāṇi sarvasamayān pālaya svāhā.* “World-Honored One! ”

Furthermore, if there should be anyone who upholds the names of the seven Buddhas, recollects the merits of those Buddhas' original vows, and likewise upholds this mantra, reading, reciting, and expounding it, I shall cause that person's wishes to be fulfilled, leaving them lacking in nothing.

If you wish to see me and inquire about good and evil, you should transcribe this sutra, fashion seven images of the Buddha along with an image of Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva, and place the relics of the Buddha within the bodies of all these images. Before these images, perform various offerings as previously described, prostrating, circumambulating, and making reverent worship.

One should give rise to a mind of loving-kindness and compassion toward all sentient beings, observe the eightfold precepts, bathe for purification three times each day, and wear different sets of robes for those three periods. From the eighth to the fifteenth day of the bright fortnight, one should recite the mantra one hundred and eight times every day with an undistracted mind.
"I shall manifest my own body within your dreams, converse with you, and fulfill all that you seek.
At that time, there were bodhisattvas in the great assembly who all cried out: "Excellent!"
Excellent, Vajrapāṇi! This dhāraṇī is inconceivable; it is indeed well-spoken.
Then the seven Tathāgatas spoke these words:

"We shall protect this divine mantra you have spoken, desiring to benefit all sentient beings so that they may all attain peace and happiness, their aspirations fulfilled, and ensuring that this mantra does not vanish from the world."
At that time, the seven Buddhas addressed the bodhisattvas, Śakra, Brahmā, and the Four Heavenly Kings, saying:

"We now entrust this divine mantra, along with this scripture, to you all. In future ages, during the final five hundred years when the Dharma is about to perish, you must all protect and uphold this sutra. The power and benefits of this sutra are exceedingly great; it can eliminate all transgressions and ensure that all virtuous aspirations are fulfilled."
"Do not bestow this sutra upon sentient beings of meager merit who slander the True Dharma or disparage the worthy and holy ones, lest the Dharma be swiftly extinguished.

At that time, the Seven World-Honored Buddhas of the East, seeing that this great assembly had accomplished what was to be done and their karmic conditions were fully matured, and that they no longer harbored any doubts, each returned to his own land; from their seats, they suddenly vanished.
At that time, the Venerable Ānanda rose from his seat, prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, knelt with his right knee on the ground, joined his palms in reverence, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
"What should this sutra be named?
How should we receive and uphold it?
The Buddha told Ānanda:

"This sutra is titled 'The Supreme Adornment of the Merit of the Original Vows of the Seven Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas'; it is also titled 'The Questions of Mañjuśrī'; it is also titled 'The Merit of the Original Vows of the Tathāgata Bhaiṣajyaguru Vaidūryaprabha'; it is also titled 'The Essential Aspirations of the Vajradhara Bodhisattvas'; it is also titled 'Purifying All Karmic Obstructions'; it is also titled 'The Fulfillment of All Wishes and Seekings'; and it is also titled 'The Aspirations and Protective Sustenance of the Twelve Great Generals. You should uphold these names."

When the Blessed One had finished speaking this sutra, the great bodhisattvas and the assembly of śrāvakas, along with the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and the entire great assembly, having heard what the Buddha taught, were all greatly rejoiced; they believed, accepted, and practiced it accordingly.
